Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

flexible adjective

bending easily without breaking

also pliable, pliant, supple, bendy, flexibility

classical

Verg. G. 4.558: lentīs … rāmīs
Ov. F. 4.435: lentō … ē vīmine
Phaedr. 3.6.6 (Lewis & Short)

lentus, lenta, lentum

pliant, bending, supple

The everyday word for a branch, an osier, a whip that bends. It has other common senses: sticky or tough, and above all slow, sluggish, at ease (lentus in umbrā, Verg. E. 1.4), so let the thing that bends make the sense clear (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • flexibilis, flexibile — that can be bent; of a voice or a mind, pliant, adaptable

    also used · classical · Ov. Am. 3.3.29: arcus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 10.11.1: nihil nōn flexibile ad bonitātem (Lewis & Short)

    The word for flexibility of mind or manner: a voice (Cic. N.D. 2.146), a person open to persuasion; in a bad sense, fickle (quid potest esse tam flexibile, Cic. Lael. 92).

  • flexilis, flexile — pliant, pliable

    also used · classical · Ov. M. 5.383: cornu (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 16.219: ulmus et fraxinus (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. flexible

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.; in prose Plin.)

Examples

  • flectitur obsequiō curvātus ab arbore rāmus: frangis, sī vīrēs experiēre tuās

    a branch bends from the tree if you go along with it; try your strength on it and you’ll break itOv. Ars 2.179–180

  • jamque arbore summā cōnfluere et lentīs ūvam dēmittere rāmīs

    and now they gather at the treetop and hang like a bunch of grapes from the bending branchesVerg. G. 4.557–558

  • haec implet lentō calathōs ē vīmine nexōs

    one fills baskets woven of pliant osierOv. F. 4.435

See also bend, soft, snap.
